title: autopilot.py status prints the manager's state in one capped command, and --hook under 1000 characters
goal: autopilot.py status prints the runners (sprint, worktree, pid, alive or exit cause, from what runner-status reads), each active sprint's counts and next item (backlog.py horizon data), the operator's pending gates, the unratified autopilot decisions and the last tick's actions from _cache/autopilot/state.json and ticks.jsonl when those files exist (a missing file prints nothing for that part and is not an error), capped (a count and the first few per section); autopilot.py status --hook prints the same in under 1000 characters, always exits 0, never writes a file and never fails the session; tests in _tools/test_autopilot.py name autopilot_status: a planted runner record, sprint, pending gate and tick file print each part, the cap holds on a long list, --hook stays under 1000 characters and exits 0 with no state at all. The SessionStart hook and the PreCompact block in .claude/settings.json are a separate task that needs the user's explicit yes.
